assessment: This study focusses on a little understood cell type, the hair cell , in the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis. It shows that the POU-IV transcription factor is required for the maturation of these likely mechanosensory neurons and activates a wide array of mechanosensory effector proteins. Because POU-IV transcription factors also play essential roles for the differentiation of mechanoreceptors in many bilaterian phyla, this suggests an evolutionarily ancient role of POU-IV in regulating mechanosensory identity.
